name: Open X-Embodiment
summary: Open X-Embodiment aggregates 60 existing datasets from 34 research labs into a single standardized format covering more than a million real robot trajectories across 22 embodiments and 500+ skills. The unglamorous work of format unification is what made every subsequent open generalist policy — Octo, OpenVLA, RDT-1B — trainable at all.
innovation: A shared data schema that made heterogeneous robot datasets mutually trainable in one batch.
Community coordination at a scale robotics had never previously achieved.
matters: The ImageNet moment for manipulation: the common substrate the open field trains on.
limits: Severely imbalanced across labs and robots, with inconsistent camera setups and language annotation quality.
Overwhelmingly single-arm tabletop data, so bimanual and dexterous coverage is thin.
lineage: The pooling of RT-1, BridgeData and dozens of other lab datasets into one corpus.
